# Iterative deterministic regex continuations

Baseline: accepted 3d7aa6ae, source f1ebb4d1a2249bf68f6a2e648c67f3781f286948f133d52587990be7d9708e8e; native PGO analysis 73.4727G versus PHP 10.3379G. Sole integrator owns regex.rs for the only active implementation.

Evidence: exact preceding accepted PGO profile assigns 1.1581G self instructions to match_seq_from and 15,277,605 entries to its grouped function identities. Public Regex entry functions cost 4.2762G inclusive, with 3.3435G entering match_seq_from. Recursive inclusive edges are overlapping and cannot be summed as a 23G regex budget. Pure consuming/anchor atoms currently call match_rest then re-enter the large Rust matcher for the next atom, despite having no state to roll back.

Outcome/hypothesis: advance every deterministic atom's existing continuation through a Rust loop within the same activation. Retain existing recursive boundaries for alternation, groups, quantifiers, capture restore, MARK/control and all rollback-bearing nodes. This removes ordinary function entry/return and rest-copy work, without pattern recognition, new guards, allocations or unsafe. Empty sequences may advance the same continuation.

Semantics: preserve budget/error observation at every matcher step, ACCEPT before continuation, exact character/Unicode/anchor flags, capture participation/restoration, recursion-budget increments, backtracking order, MARK/control, lookarounds/subroutines and public preg errors. LocalFlags keeps its existing scoped recursion. The linked continuation's borrowed nodes remain within their existing enclosing Rust activations; no references to self-mutating continuation storage are introduced. No public ABI/feature/JIT change.

Gates: exact source/binary preservation, default focused regex engine and preg suites; PHP and baseline differential fixtures for global/nested continuations, empty alternatives, captures, local flags, control and limits. Early same-policy opt-level-one native phase comparison against the exact named-types exploratory binary must preserve outputs and reduce whole analysis instructions at least 0.5% before broader matrix or fresh PGO. Accepted release requires >=0.5% independently confirmed PGO reduction with focused no-default/all-feature correctness, independent controls, RSS/code-size and cleanup. Reject changed semantics, growing stack/heap or the early instruction filter; remove the whole source change and choose another quantified cost. Native architecture evidence remains x86-64 only.

Existing differential exception: nested output line 15 carries the previously documented PRUNE PHP mismatch in performance-phpstan-regex-continuations-samples.json. The initial broad PHP-equality gate remains a failure. An explicit supported-line validation must preserve every baseline/candidate line and all other PHP lines, while retaining PRUNE as a known failed PHP contract, never counting it as a pass. This does not relax any candidate semantic-change rejection.
